Enter the address you open AdGuard Home\'s web interface on, and the username and password you sign in with there.
Connects to %1$s, and only to this address
Without http://, AdCtrl uses HTTPS. AdCtrl only ever connects to the address you enter here.
That doesn\'t look like a web address.
Plain http:// is only allowed for addresses on your own network (like 192.168.x.x or adguard.lan), because AdGuard Home sends your password with every request. Use https:// for this address.
Defaults to the address, like \"Primary\" or \"Secondary\"
Enter the password again: it\'s only reused for the same address and username.
Allow plain HTTP for this server
Your password and query log travel unencrypted on your network
Only for addresses on your own network. A name like adguard.lan must also point to a private address, or AdCtrl won\'t connect. HTTPS is safer: see the README\'s recommended setup.

AdCtrl will talk to %1$s without encryption. AdGuard Home sends your username and password with every request, and the query log shows what everyone on your network visits, so anyone who can watch your network can read both. Only do this on a network you trust.
%1$s uses a certificate your phone doesn\'t know, like a self-signed certificate.
%1$s now presents a different certificate from the one you trusted. Only continue if you replaced or renewed it yourself.
Check that this SHA-256 fingerprint matches your certificate (on the server: openssl x509 -in cert.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256):
From now on AdCtrl only accepts this exact certificate from this server.
Switch, add or remove AdGuard Home servers
AdCtrl forgets this server and deletes its saved password from the phone. Nothing changes on the server itself.
Hide every action that changes something on this server, and refuse to send one
Can\'t reach %1$s. Check the address and that your phone is on a network that can reach it.
%1$s presents a different certificate from the one you trusted. AdCtrl stopped connecting to protect your password.
Wrong username or password. After several wrong passwords (5 by default), AdGuard Home blocks sign-ins from your address for a while (15 minutes by default), even with the right password.
%1$s answered, but not like AdGuard Home. Check the address and port: it\'s the one you open AdGuard Home\'s web interface on.
%1$s answered with a redirect. AdCtrl never follows redirects, so enter the address AdGuard Home actually runs on (often its https:// address).
%1$s redirects to %2$s. AdCtrl never follows redirects, so enter that address instead (often the https:// one).
This server runs AdGuard Home %1$s. AdCtrl needs %2$s or newer: update AdGuard Home, then tap Retry.
AdCtrl won\'t use plain HTTP for %1$s: it\'s only allowed for addresses on your own network, with the server\'s HTTP switch on.
AdCtrl only connects to the servers you added, so this request wasn\'t sent.
This server is in read-only mode, so nothing was changed. Turn read-only mode off to make changes.
Cancelled: the change wasn\'t confirmed with your fingerprint or screen lock.
